faq.question: What is there to do in Buenos Aires this weekend?
faq.answer: BA Eventos lists the weekend's theater, live music, fairs, and poetry in Buenos Aires, from Friday to Sunday. Each listing shows the time, venue, and neighborhood, and links to the source. The site focuses on independent culture and only lists events from the sources it follows.

faq.question: Can I use BA Eventos in English?
faq.answer: Yes. The site has an English version, and the chat answers in English. Many event names stay in Spanish because the venues post in Spanish.

faq.question: What does «a la gorra» mean?
faq.answer: «A la gorra» means there's no set ticket price. At the end, someone passes the hat and you give what you can. BA Eventos doesn't count these events as free.

faq.question: Is there a list of free events?
faq.answer: Yes. [Free events in Buenos Aires this week](/en/free-events-this-week) lists only events with no charge.

faq.question: What free things are there to do in Buenos Aires this week?
faq.answer: This page lists every free event BA Eventos has for the next 7 days: theater, live music, fairs, exhibitions, and readings at venues and cultural centers in Buenos Aires. Each listing shows the time, venue, and neighborhood, and links to the source.

faq.question: Do I need to book free events?
faq.answer: It depends on the event. Some ask you to register or get a free ticket, and others are open to everyone. Open the listing's link to see what the source asks for.

faq.question: What's the difference between free and «a la gorra»?
faq.answer: A free event has no charge. At an event «a la gorra», there's no set price, and someone passes the hat at the end for you to give what you can. BA Eventos labels those events «A la gorra» and keeps them off the free list.
